title: The New Primitives: Building AI Native Software — Kwindla Kramer, Daily
talk_summary: Kwindla Kramer gives a historical tour of computing (Vannevar Bush, Knowledge Navigator, Minority Report UI) to argue that today's 'agents' are like 1995 web pages and that AI-native software will be built on multi-model harnesses with rich context and progressive tool disclosure.

takeaways.what_they_do: Sub-agents compress their context asynchronously so the main agent loop never blocks on summarization, keeping long-running interactions responsive.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Gradient Bang demonstrates several patterns for AI sub agents such as asynchronous non-blocking context compression.

takeaways.what_they_do: Spawn persistent sub-agents that inherit and share the parent's context rather than starting cold, so work continues across many steps without re-priming.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Long-running sub agents that share context.

takeaways.what_they_do: Expose only the tools/skills relevant to the current step, loading more on demand, to keep the prompt token-efficient.

takeaways.technique: Dynamic UI generation by the agent
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent generates interface elements on the fly in response to user requests instead of shipping fixed screens.
